findings.finding: At the Baird conference on 2026-09-15, management said hospital and SNF costs are rising, driven mainly by a claims-system transition that left 2025 hospital bills lagging (i.e. late-arriving prior-period claims) and secondarily by longer SNF stays; the CEO called it 'messy and noisy' but 'settling'. No dollar figure was given and the FY guide was not changed. The stock fell 16%. TD Cowen then cut H2 adj. EBITDA by about $16m on inpatient utilization (Oct 12), which would put FY at about $138m against the $145-163m guide, and William Blair expects Q3 to show cost-trend problems. Q3 is the first quantified look: adverse prior-period development and the Q3 MBR against a $20-30m EBITDA guide, plus whether FY adj. EBITDA is cut below $145m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (2026-07-30): beat the top of the guide but signalled heavier H2 spending (only ~30% of FY EBITDA in H2); the stock fell 20.2%. Sept 15 cost commentary: -16%. Beats and raises on this name have recently been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is partly priced: -16% on Sept 15 and estimate cuts. The size is not, because no dollar figure for the 2025 claims lag or the SNF pressure exists anywhere public, and street EPS ranges from -$0.04 to +$0.04. A fully priced cost miss would show as an EBITDA consensus visibly below the $145m guide low end and an EPS spread that had converged; neither is visible.
findings.independence: TD Cowen's H2 EBITDA cut of about $16m on inpatient utilization (Barchart via Webull, 2026-10-12, https://www.webull.com/news/15736444743656448). William Blair's downgrade expecting Q3 cost-trend problems (https://www.tikr.com/blog/alignment-healthcare-sinks-20-as-medicare-plan-downgraded-humana-and-clover-soar). Both are analyst reads, partly of the same management remarks, so they are one fact here, not two.

findings.finding: Large MA peers that reported Q3 2026 after Alignment last spoke showed benign or improving cost trend. UnitedHealth's Q3 medical care ratio was 88.4% against 89.9% a year earlier, with $610m favorable 2026 reserve development, and it raised its FY guide (8-K, Oct 13). Elevance's benefit expense ratio was 90.6%, 70bp better, with Medicare Advantage named as a main driver (Oct 21). Humana affirmed its FY guide in an Oct 13 8-K while closing Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of ALHC trading on peer read-through at its own print. ALHC fell 14% with peers on the January 2026 rate proposal, so sector factors do move it.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer prints came after the William Blair and TD Cowen cuts (Oct 9-12), and ALHC's -2.3% 5-day drift shows no relief rally on them. The street's Q3 caution on ALHC predates the industry data. If the market had priced a benign industry trend into ALHC, the stock would have run up into the print instead of sitting at its pre-stars level. Sized small because it is a proxy: the incumbents' MCR gains come from benefit cuts and membership shedding, while ALHC is a 30%-growth plan whose stated problem is company-specific (its claims system).
findings.independence: Elevance Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001156039/000115603926000068/a3q2026elvearningsrelease.htm, 2026-10-21) and Humana's Oct 13 guidance affirmation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049071/000004907126000060/hum-20261013.htm) are separate companies and documents.

findings.finding: HCA's Q3 2026 same-facility admissions rose 2.7% (equivalent admissions +3.0%, ER visits +5.1%) against +2.1% a year earlier: slightly firmer hospital inpatient volume. That is the line TD Cowen flagged for ALHC (inpatient utilization).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific; inpatient costs drove the Sept 15 -16% move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an all-payer national hospital series; nobody prices ALHC's Southern California MA admissions off it. Small because it is a proxy, and the broader MA payer series (UNH, ELV) point the other way, so it is sized below them.
findings.independence: TD Cowen's inpatient-utilization cut (https://www.webull.com/news/15736444743656448) points the same way but is an analyst read, not data.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08 CMS rated contract H3815 (California HMO, about 75% of members) 3.5 stars for 2027, down from 4.0, so the share of members in 4+ star plans falls from 98% to 25%. In its 8-K Alignment said there is no revenue impact in 2026 or 2027 and that provider risk-sharing will offset part of the 2028 quality-bonus hit, without giving a number. Its own D.D.C. complaint (Oct 9) puts the loss at more than $200m of 2028 payments, against FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance with a $154m midpoint. The Q3 call is the first place management can quantify the hit net of risk-sharing and mitigation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Star news on 2026-10-09: about -19-20% premarket, then -13.4% on the session and +8.6% the next day. Since then the stock has fully retraced to its Oct 6 level ($8.30).
findings.why_not_priced: The gross figure (>$200m) sits in a litigation complaint, which is an advocacy document; the net figure after provider risk-sharing has not been given anywhere. The full retrace back to $8.30 says the market is not pricing the gross $200m against a ~$154m EBITDA base. It also leaves room both for relief (a net hit well under $100m) and for a second leg down (a 2027-2028 framework below the street). Sign near zero, wide range.
findings.independence: Healthcare Dive (2026-10-13, https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/alignment-lawsuit-2027-medicare-advantage-star-ratings-cms/832774/) reports the >$200m figure and the 98%->25% share from the complaint. That is the same underlying document, not independent.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call, management agreed with an analyst's ~20% enrollment-growth framing for 2027. For 2027 it is adding 10 counties in four states (77 plans in 55 counties, including San Antonio, Charlotte and California's Central Valley) and adding Hoag and Astrana to its network. Competitors are retreating: Humana is exiting plans covering ~600k MA members for 2027 and UnitedHealthcare discontinuing plans covering ~390k. 2027 benefits were bid on 2026 stars (4.0 on H3815), so the 3.5-star rating does not reduce 2027 benefit richness. The Q3 call (AEP opened Oct 15) is the first read on 2027 growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Membership-led beats (Q2 +31.5% members) did not protect the stock (-20.2%); growth commentary has paid little on this name lately. Feb 2025 (+16.5%) was the last strongly positive print, on a guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades at about $8, about $1.8bn or less of market value on roughly 300k members, which prices little 2027 growth. A priced 20% growth path would show a valuation per member above the ~$7,500-8,000 TD Cowen cited. Partly offset because H3815 shows 3.5 stars in Plan Finder during this AEP, which may dent sales; resolved here into one net-small positive.
findings.independence: Humana's 2027 exits (Becker's, https://www.beckerspayer.com/payer/medicare-advantage/humana-to-exit-medicare-advantage-plans-covering-600000-members-in-2027/); Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15341674950829056) for the 20% framing. These are different documents.

findings.finding: Revenue line: Alignment has beaten its revenue guide and consensus by about 1-2% in each of the last four quarters (Q2: $1,335.6m, 'surpassing high end of guidance across all key metrics'). The Q3 guide of $1.30-1.32bn equals the $1.31bn consensus, so a top-line beat and membership at or above 297.5k are likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats were sold on the last three prints (-20.2, -10.1, -5.9). The line does not pay on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: a consistent beater's revenue beat is expected. Kept at near zero because the reaction function vetoes it.
findings.independence: The Q2 release headline (https://ir.alignmenthealth.com/news-releases/news-release-details/alignment-healthcare-reports-second-quarter-2026-results) shares the history but is a different document.
